additions.reason: Line 78 of the source text states: 'הַנְּשָׁמָה, שֶׁהוּא הַטּוֹב, הוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת.' This uses the equational formula 'she-hu ha-tov' (that it is the good) as a bechina-identification: the soul = the good = what floats above all worlds. The context (§ח, the sea-creature midrash) explains that the 'light creature' that floats on the sea = the neshamah = the good that is above the four worlds. While the dataset has 'kol ha-tov = nishmat Yisrael' (edge 2230, ref=17), it does NOT have 'neshamah = ha-tov' as an explicit separate bechina edge. The concept 'neshamah' here belongs in Package 4 (the chokhmah/intellect cluster) because the midrash is about the soul's relationship to the four worlds traversed by divine wisdom, and the 'good' (= neshamah) is what proper eating at the mizbeach protects. This addition would create the edge: נְשָׁמָה ↔ הַטּוֹב (or alternatively: נְשָׁמָה ↔ כָּל הַטּוֹב, connecting to the Package 2 node).
